article.title: NFL EDGE Sunday Morning Brief
article.dek: The board finally flipped to Week 10 overnight — Munich inactives are in, the 49ers are back to -4.5, and the app has three live cards for Sunday.

items.headline: Lead: The board finally flipped — Week 10 is live
paragraphs: Overnight, the board flipped. Saturday night it was still showing the November 2 board. This morning it is Week 10, fresh, with thirteen Sunday games and three live headline cards.

That changes today completely. The numbers in this brief are real Week 10 numbers, not last week's leftovers. Munich kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, the 1:00 p.m. ET window follows, and the nightcap is Steelers at Bengals at 8:20 p.m. ET.
items.takeaway: The board flipped overnight — Week 10 is live, the cards are real, and Munich kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET.

items.headline: Injuries: Munich inactives are in — Brown, Stevenson and St. Brown all play
paragraphs: Munich inactives landed early, and the news is good for both sides. Patriots receiver A.J. Brown and running back Rhamondre Stevenson are both active after being listed questionable. Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and running back Sione Vaki are active too.

The Lions are short elsewhere: cornerback D.J. Reed, center Cade Mays and safety Kerby Joseph did not travel and are out. The Patriots are without running back TreVeyon Henderson, who went on injured reserve Saturday, plus lineman Ben Brown, cornerback Carlton Davis III, safety Brenden Schooler and lineman Walter Rouse.

The rest of the board holds from Saturday: Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III is out with a groin injury at Atlanta. Deshaun Watson starts for Cleveland, Kirk Cousins starts for Minnesota, and Drew Lock starts for Seattle with Sam Darnold out again. The app's expected starters match all of that.

Two more names from the week: Rams receiver Puka Nacua went on injured reserve Thursday and is out at least four games. Packers running back Josh Jacobs had finger surgery Monday and could miss up to three weeks. Jets receiver Garrett Wilson is still questionable against Buffalo, and the Saints activated running back Travis Etienne from injured reserve — he is questionable against Carolina.
Inactives for the later games land about 90 minutes before kickoff. If your bet depends on a questionable name, that is the moment that decides it.

items.takeaway: Brown, Stevenson and St. Brown are all active in Munich; Walker is out for Kansas City, Watson and Cousins start, and the later inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: final check — nothing flagged, same as last night
paragraphs: The morning weather check is clean. No outdoor game is forecast to reach 15 mph sustained wind, the line that usually matters.

Munich is calm and cloudy, 48 degrees, wind barely 2 mph. MetLife has the strongest gusts at 22 mph, and Cleveland has the only rain chance at 33% light rain — neither reaches the line that changes a game. This is weather to note, not weather to bet on.
items.takeaway: No wind flag anywhere on Sunday — Munich is calm, MetLife has the strongest gusts, Cleveland has the only rain chance, and none of it reaches the line that matters.

items.headline: Sunday: thirteen games, starting in Munich at 9:30 a.m. ET
paragraphs: Thirteen games today. Munich opens the day at 9:30 a.m. ET, the big 1:00 p.m. ET window carries nine games, then Seahawks at Raiders and Rams at Cardinals in the late window, 49ers at Cowboys at 4:25 p.m. ET, and Steelers at Bengals at 8:20 p.m. ET. Chargers at Ravens closes the week Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET.
The Jaguars are still the week's biggest favorite at -10.5 at Tennessee, and 49ers at Cowboys still carries the highest total at 55.5.
items.takeaway: Thirteen games Sunday, starting with Patriots at Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET — the Jaguars are the biggest favorite at -10.5 and 49ers at Cowboys carries the week's highest total at 55.5.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Three live cards — and what each one is actually for
paragraphs: Hit Rate has Seattle moneyline at -285 on DraftKings. The app gives Seattle about a 70% chance to win. That is the pick most likely to win — and the price says so. At -285, every $2.85 you risk wins $1. Hit Rate is about winning, not about value. The app's own tutorial says it plainly: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.

Balanced has Cleveland +4.5 at -108 on DraftKings. The app gives the Browns about a 50.5% chance to cover, with a small edge of about 1.1%. This is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much. It is a good starting point if you are new to this.

Value has Carolina moneyline at +114 on FanDuel. The app gives the Panthers about a 52% chance to win outright, with an edge of about 1.1%. That is the model's plus-EV play. It is marked target-only, so watch the price: if your book is offering worse than +114, run it through Check before you touch it.
items.takeaway: Seattle moneyline is the likeliest winner, Cleveland +4.5 is the middle ground, and Carolina moneyline is the model's plus-EV play — use each card for what it is.

items.headline: The Jaguars are -10.5. The app sees a much closer game.
paragraphs: Jacksonville is the week's biggest favorite at -10.5 at Tennessee. But the app's expected margin for that game is only about 5.8 points. The market and the app are a long way apart here.

That does not make Tennessee a bet on its own. It means the app thinks this game is closer than the price says. If you like the Jaguars, do not pay -10.5 blind — type your book's line into Check and let the app run it back through the model and the evaluator. If your book has a better number, Check will tell you.
items.takeaway: The market has Jacksonville -10.5 but the app's margin is only about 5.8 — a big gap, so Check your price before you pay it.

items.headline: The quarterbacks check out — and inactives can still change the number
paragraphs: The app's expected starters line up with the morning news: Watson for Cleveland, Cousins for Minnesota, Lock for Seattle. The board is pricing the right quarterbacks this morning.

But a questionable starter is still a moving number. When inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff and the starter changes, the old verdict is dead. Run the new number through Check — the app re-runs it through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The app is pricing the right quarterbacks this morning — but if inactives change a starter, the old verdict is dead, so Check the new number.

items.headline: Learn the Game: juice — the price of placing the bet
paragraphs: Juice, also called the vig, is the book's cut on a bet. It is why most standard lines are -110 instead of even money.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you bet a spread at -110. You risk $1.10 to win $1. That extra 10 cents is the juice — the book keeps it when you win, and it is gone when you lose. Two bets at -110 need you to win more than half the time just to break even, because the juice is working against you on every ticket.

That is why the price matters as much as the pick. A good pick at -110 and the same pick at -130 are not the same bet. Before you take any price, run it through Check and see what the app says about it.
items.takeaway: Juice is the book's cut — at -110 you risk $1.10 to win $1, so the price is part of the bet, and Check tells you whether your price is worth it.

items.headline: The 49ers are back to -4.5, and the totals kept climbing
paragraphs: The 49ers dipped to -3.5 on Saturday and are back to -4.5 at DraftKings this morning. Their total at Dallas climbed from 53.5 to 55.5 — still the week's highest.

The Munich total moved up too, from 49.5 to 50.5. The Bills moved from -7 to -8.5 at the Jets, and that total jumped from 46.5 to 50.5. The Texans at Browns total is up from 38.5 to 40.5, and the Jaguars moved from -10 to -10.5 with their total up from 45.5 to 46.5.

The board caught all of this — it refreshed fresh this morning. But your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel by default. If your number is different from the one here, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: 49ers -4.5 again, Munich total up to 50.5, Bills -8.5 and the totals climbing — the board caught it all, and Check is there if your book's number is different.

items.headline: Today's job: Munich is already decided — wait only for the names you need
paragraphs: Munich kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET and its inactives are already out, so there is nothing left to wait on there. For the rest of the day, inactives land about 90 minutes before each kickoff.

Wait only for inactives if your bet depends on a questionable player. Otherwise, if your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet it now. A good number today beats a hoped-for number later — waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too.
One more thing: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too. A tracker that only holds winners is a souvenir, not a record.
items.takeaway: Munich is decided — wait only for the inactives your bet actually needs, bet a good number now if Check says bet, and log the losers too.
